candidates.source_name: Registr smluv (ISRS) – public web portal, smlouvy.gov.cz
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory Czech contract register operated for the state (originally MV CR, since 1 Apr 2023 under DIA). All public bodies must publish private-law contracts above CZK 50,000 excl. VAT within 30 days; non-publication renders the contract ineffective. This is the executed, priced counterpart to a tender notice: who actually won, at what value, plus amendments (dodatky) for bank account services, payment/acquiring services, POS terminals, card issuing, cash handling.
candidates.legal_status: official public register under Act No. 340/2015 Sb.; metadata published as open data; contains personal data under GDPR
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the bulk open-data XML dumps over HTML scraping; use the web UI only for spot checks and for pulling individual contract PDFs by ID.
candidates.discovered_via_method: cs seed search on contract-register + bank account contract terms
queries_used: registr smluv smlouva o vedeni uctu banka mesto

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, curated dataset or portal exists that isolates banking/payment-services contracts within the Czech contract register. Searching 'registr smluv platebni terminaly dodavatel smlouva' returned the register's generic pages and unrelated contracts rather than any sectoral view.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector filtering must be built by us, from free-text subject fields plus a supplier ICO watchlist; no ready-made banking slice was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Implies real engineering effort (keyword + ICO + CPV-style classification) before the register yields a usable banking/payments series, and implies recall risk from inconsistent free-text subjects.

negative_findings.description: The register's exemptions regime — notably the banking-secrecy carve-out discussed in Czech legal commentary, plus redaction of commercially sensitive terms (files named *_RED.PDF) — removes or obscures part of the bank-side contract content.
negative_findings.result_summary: Pricing schedules and some counterparty terms in banking contracts may be redacted or the contract exempt entirely; presence in the register is not proof of full disclosure.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any pricing benchmark drawn from these documents must be flagged as a lower bound on visibility, not a complete market picture.

negative_findings.description: The official register publishes bulk monthly XML dumps and publication (write) interfaces, but I found no documented official read/query REST API for ad-hoc searching. Programmatic search appears to require either local ingestion of the dumps or the third-party Hlidac statu API.
negative_findings.result_summary: Official access pattern is bulk-download-and-index; ad-hoc programmatic search depends on a third party.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Creates a dependency: either we run our own index (cost, but full control) or we depend on Hlidac's availability and terms for query-time access.

negative_findings.description: Official documentation states that historical XML dumps are rewritten retroactively when a contract is modified or made inaccessible, and that all versions of a withdrawn contract are removed from historical dumps.
negative_findings.result_summary: The register is not an append-only archive; past snapshots can silently change or lose records.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Longitudinal series can shift under us and disappearances can be mistaken for market changes; we must keep our own timestamped, hashed snapshots and diff them.

negative_findings.description: data.isrs.cz is cited in the official open-data documentation as the dump directory listing, but I did not independently fetch it in this pass. registrysmluv.cz's operator, coverage claim (8.3m contracts) and terms of service were likewise not verified.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both recorded with reduced confidence rather than as confirmed live sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids overstating availability of a fallback mirror and of a commercial index whose licence terms could forbid automated collection.

negative_findings.description: The official open-data page states explicitly that the dataset contains personal data within the meaning of GDPR, that the recipient becomes a controller, and that records made inaccessible must be deleted from downstream systems.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bulk ingestion carries an affirmative data-protection obligation, including honouring retroactive redactions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The collector needs a deletion/reconciliation routine and a documented lawful basis before we ingest at scale — this is a build requirement, not a footnote.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching for the Czech contract register returned mostly the register's own pages, Wikipedia and generic legal-dictionary noise; no substantive English analytical coverage of Czech disclosed banking contracts was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: English is usable for framing and legal context only; all real discovery in this cell must be done in Czech.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that any collector or analyst working this cell needs Czech-language keyword lists; an English-only pipeline would miss essentially everything.

coverage_gaps.description: No validated Czech keyword/CPV taxonomy yet exists for identifying banking and payment contracts in free-text 'predmet smlouvy' fields (e.g. 'vedeni bezneho uctu', 'platebni terminal', 'akceptace platebnich karet', 'zpracovani hotovosti', 'bankovni sluzby', 'platebni brana', 'POS terminal', 'ekvajring/acquiring').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and precision/recall-test a Czech keyword + ICO + CPV-code classifier against a hand-labelled sample of a few hundred register records before running any market sizing.

coverage_gaps.description: The banking/payments supplier watchlist (ICOs for Ceska sporitelna, Komercni banka, CSOB, Moneta, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit CZ, Fio, J&T, plus acquirers/terminal vendors such as Global Payments, Worldline, Monet+, Printec and gateway providers) was not yet resolved to ICO in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve the full actor list to ICO via ARES, then run ICO-keyed queries against Hlidac subject pages and the ISRS dumps to build each supplier's public-sector contract book.

coverage_gaps.description: How amendments (dodatky) are linked to parent contracts in the register metadata was not established. Amendments are where real value drift and contract extensions appear, which is central to this cell's rationale.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Inspect the dump XSD and a sample of banking contract families to determine whether a reliable parent-child key exists; if not, design a matching heuristic on parties + subject + date.

coverage_gaps.description: The join between the contract register (executed contracts) and the tender/award registers (NEN, VVZ, TED) was not investigated in this cell, so we cannot yet trace a notice through to its signed contract and value.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Coordinate with the tender-portal cell; evaluate whether Datlab/Hlidac already provide the notice-to-contract linkage, or whether it must be built on ICO + date + value matching.

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage of state-owned and quasi-public banks/entities (e.g. Ceska exportni banka, Narodni rozvojova banka, Ceska posta) as either buyers or suppliers of payment services in the register was not probed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run ICO-keyed passes for these entities; check whether commercial-activity exemptions reduce their disclosure.

coverage_gaps.description: Terms of use and rate limits for the two key third-party layers (Hlidac statu API, registrysmluv.cz) were not read, and no API token was obtained.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Read both ToS, register a Hlidac API token, and record permitted use in the source registry before any automated collection.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival strategy exists to counter the register's retroactive rewriting of historical dumps and withdrawal of contracts, and no third-party immutable archive of the register was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up our own hashed monthly snapshot archive from day one; investigate whether Hlidac or a web archive retains withdrawn records that the official dumps drop.

brief: The Czech contract register (ISRS, smlouvy.gov.cz, operated by DIA since April 2023 under Act 340/2015 Sb.) is the anchor source for this cell: publication above CZK 50,000 excl. VAT within 30 days is a condition of a contract taking effect, which makes it unusually complete and gives us the signed, priced counterpart to any tender notice — including the actual PDFs of municipal bank account and banking-services agreements. The practical architecture is bulk-first: monthly XML dumps at data.smlouvy.gov.cz (index.xml, XSD-validated, hashed) for the metadata backbone, attachment PDFs pulled and OCR'd for pricing detail, with Hlidac statu providing the full-text/OCR search, per-ICO contract books and risk analytics that the official portal lacks, and ARES supplying ICO resolution for a banking/payments supplier watchlist. Three constraints shape any collector built on this: the banking-secrecy and commercial-sensitivity exemptions redact part of exactly the content we want, the dumps are rewritten retroactively so historical series can change or lose records, and the data is explicitly GDPR personal data with a downstream deletion obligation. No ready-made banking/payments slice of the register exists in either Czech or English, so sector classification and amendment-to-parent linkage are ours to build and validate.
